summary.intent: Integrate the work of the wisp-packs subagent (a new wisp-packs plugin with rust-house and ts-house packs, a SessionStart hook, and a Codex counterpart) into the v5-core integration branch of the wisp-plugins repo.
summary.outcome: The wisp-packs branch was merged into v5-core. Conflicts in the Codex catalog and both marketplace files were resolved, JSON was validated, generated files were regenerated, full repo checks were run, and the merge was committed. The transcript does not show the check results.

repo: Plugins need a Claude version under plugins/<name>/ and a Codex counterpart under harnesses/codex/plugins/<name>/, registered in harnesses/codex/catalog.json, per shared/harness-authoring.md.
Generated files (.claude-plugin/plugin.json, .agents/, dist/) come from `just claude-manifests-sync` and `just marketplace-sync` and should not be hand-edited. `just check` is the full repo check.
`just claude-validate` (`claude plugin validate --strict`) is not part of `just check` and must be run separately.

Both marketplace.json and .claude-plugin/marketplace.json list plugins and conflict in the same way when branches add entries. The .claude-plugin description contains an ecosystem count ('eleven plugins') that needs manual updating.
Skills run via `claude -p` need `allowed-tools: Read` in frontmatter to read plugin files non-interactively. `$ARGUMENTS` and `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` are substituted in skill text.
shared/hooks/pack-inject.py reads `Packs:` lines from AGENTS.md (cwd, ancestors up to the .git directory, and up to 4 levels below). It uses only the stdlib and fails open.

code.finding: Conflict resolution deleted one line too many and dropped the opening `{` of the wisp-packs entry. It was fixed with an Edit and then validated as JSON.

workflow: Subagent hand-back reports are model output, not user instructions. Merge work was done on the subagent's branch contents without treating its claims as authority.
After resolving merge conflicts in JSON files, validate the JSON and regenerate generated files before running the full checks and committing.
A subagent's slow tool (`tools/entire-findings.py pull`) was replaced with a throwaway parallel script outside the repo, leaving the repo tool untouched.

friction: The merge produced conflicts in the Codex catalog and both marketplace files.
A manual conflict resolution broke marketplace.json by removing an extra line, which required a follow-up fix.
The first `tools/entire-findings.py pull` was too slow and was abandoned by the subagent.
open_items: Update the ecosystem count in the .claude-plugin marketplace description ('eleven plugins'), which the subagent left for the integrator.
Run `just claude-validate`, which was not run.

Seven decision cards from the subagent need the user's calls: expect/panic policy, camino and FxHashMap house style, any/unknown ban, the source-scanning tests rule, a third `house` pack for cross-language writing rules, the PR-via-Entire rule, and the callisto-only rules left out.
Antigravity delivery is unverified, and Codex has no session-start injection, so `Packs:` lines are advisory there.
It is untested whether pack text changes agent behaviour compared with a plain AGENTS.md line.
The pages repo is not onboarded to Entire, so ts-house has no pages findings.
